evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/comparison-context.tsx:37-46 restores comparison state from localStorage: `const stored = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY); ... const parsed = JSON.parse(stored); setListings(parsed);`. The try/catch (L39-45) only guards JSON *parse* errors — it does NOT validate the parsed *shape*. Any syntactically-valid-but-non-array value in the `reality-comparison` key (legacy schema, manual edit, cross-tab corruption, e.g. `{}`, `5`, or `null`) parses fine and is fed directly into `setListings`, whose declared type is `ListingSummary[]` (L29).

Crash path is reachable and global: `listings` is consumed by the always-mounted ComparisonTray (frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonTray.tsx:16 `listings.length`, :30 `listings.map`, :53 `4 - listings.length`) and ComparisonView (ComparisonView.tsx:100/158/253/283 `.length`/`.map`). A non-array `listings` throws `listings.map is not a function` on first render of the tray, and since the tray is rendered on every page via the layout, a single corrupted localStorage entry white-screens the whole portal for that visitor until they clear storage.

Fix (frontend-only, self-contained): after JSON.parse, guard with `Array.isArray(parsed)` (and ideally filter to entries with a string `id`) before setListings; on failure fall through to the existing `localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY)` recovery branch. Mirrors the defensive shape-normalization the SSR side already does via parseListingDetail. Confidence medium: requires a corrupted/legacy storage value (not attacker-triggerable over the network), but is a real client crash with no shape guard today.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/auth/callback/page.tsx renders entirely hardcoded English on a next-intl locale-aware route (sk/cs/de/en): 'Loading...' (L66), 'Completing login...' (L144), the error heading 'Login Failed' (L130), the CTA 'Return Home' (L132-134), and the runtime error string 'Invalid state token. Please try logging in again.' (L106). The component imports no `useTranslations`/`getTranslations` (grep: 0 hits) despite living under the [locale] segment.

This is the SSO landing page every OAuth login funnels through, so a Slovak/Czech/German user completing login is shown English status + failure UI — an inconsistent, unlocalized experience on an auth-critical, high-visibility surface. It is distinct from the already-filed comparison-feature i18n gap (that sweep was scoped to components/comparison/; this is the auth flow).

Fix (frontend-only): route the five literals through `useTranslations('auth')` (or a dedicated 'auth.callback' namespace) and add the keys to the sk/cs/de/en message catalogs. Low severity (i18n gap, no functional break).
